transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-20 15:00 PST | Duration: ~52 mins | Attendees: Samir, Lina (Redwood); Jared, Priya, Marcus, Elena (NorthBay)

Summary: Quick discovery to understand model selection needs for a SaaS analytics product that will support multi-lingual query interpretation, tool-calling to internal services, and a mix of hosted + private deployment for regulated customers. They're evaluating open models and care about 64k context for long reports, plus predictable latency for interactive UI.

Topics: open model tradeoffs, context length (32k vs 64k), multilingual quality, tool-calling/func-calls, dedicated vs private deployment (VPC), security (SOC2/KMS), cost/latency trade-offs, benchmark next steps.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir with Redwood, AE. Lina, my solutions engineer is here. How's it going?
[00:08] Jared: Good thanks. Quick intros from our side — I'm Jared, CTO; Priya does ML; Marcus infra; Elena product. We're hoping to decide which model path to take and how to host it.
[00:16] Samir: Great. High level — you mentioned needing tool-calling and long context, multi-lang — did I get that right?
[00:22] Elena: Yep. We have customer support transcripts, long quarterly reports — so 30k+ tokens sometimes. Also need live actions where model calls internal endpoints to fetch user history.
[00:30] Lina: Ok, so long-context plus tool calling. Two immediate choices: larger open models tuned for long context, or smaller base models with retrieval augmentation. Wanted to ask about throughput/latency SLOs?
[00:39] Marcus: For our product interactive UI, p95 latency under 600ms is ideal. Some background jobs can be async.
[00:44] Priya: And quality: multi-lingual — Spanish and Portuguese customers are big. We need coherent responses in those languages.
[00:50] Samir: Makes sense. In practice we often recommend hybrid: Redwood Hosted for dev and burst workloads, Dedicated for predictable production, and Private/VPC for regulated accounts. For model selection, are you leaning open-source?
[01:00] Jared: Yes, cost sensitivity but we want control. Open models are preferred. Do you have benchmarks for 32k vs 64k context?
[01:07] Lina: We do. Quick caveat: 64k models are less common at high quality; you typically either use a 32k model and augment with retrieval or pick a 64k transformer variant. Latency and memory go up nonlinearly. We have a perf brief — I'll share.
[01:18] Priya: If we used retrieval, how would tool-calling work? We need the model to call a fuse service to pull sensitive PII after auth.
[01:26] Lina: Tool-calling works with both approaches. You can surface retrieved docs as context or call an internal microservice via function-calling. For PII, recommended flow is: Redwood Private in VPC, KMS for envelope encryption, and function-calls to services that run in your network. Note: I might say 'KV cash' later in the transcript, sorry for the auto-transcribe.
[01:42] Marcus: We need to be sure about KMS — HSM is a requirement for some clients. Do you support that?
[01:47] Samir: Yes, Private deployments integrate with customer KMS/HSM. We'll provide an architecture doc.
[01:51] Elena: What about prompt latency when doing tool-calls? Concerned about chaining calls.
[01:55] Lina: Chaining adds round trips. In Dedicated you can colocate the function runner to reduce latency. Also we support streaming so UI perceived latency improves.; There's a tradeoff: batching helps cost but hurts latency at p95.
[02:08] Priya: For multilingual quality, do you have recommended models?
[02:11] Lina: For Spanish/Portuguese we'd suggest testing LlamaX-extended or Mistral open variants with multilingual fine-tune. Anthropic-ish options sometimes excel but at higher cost; Cohere and Vertex were mentioned earlier — but we do per-model evals.
[02:24] Jared: Are there pre-built evals or prompt suites we can use?
[02:27] Samir: Yep — Redwood Optimize includes prompt sets and quality monitoring. We'll share a sample eval harness and a few real prompt examples.
[02:33] Marcus: On infra — if we go Private, do you orchestrate on our VPC or do we run a package?
[02:38] Lina: We support a private control plane with customer-managed networking. For fully air-gapped customers we have an on-prem package. For most regulated customers we deploy the runtime into your VPC and leave control plane connectivity minimal.
[02:48] Priya: Can we pin model versions and do canary rollouts?
[02:51] Samir: Yes, version pinning and rollouts are supported — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to smaller models if a runway is reached.
[02:58] Elena: Pricing — ballpark numbers for 64k context model on Dedicated?
[03:02] Samir: Ballpark depends on tokens and tokenization. For a 64k model on Dedicated reserved capacity, customers often commit monthly GPU hours. We'll send tailored pricing but expect materially higher unit cost vs 32k model + retrieval.
[03:15] (crosstalk)
[03:20] Jared: For the benchmark run, we want a sample that includes long docs and tool-calls — can you simulate our traffic?
[03:25] Lina: Yes — we'll work with Marcus on traffic profile. Marcus, can you provide a 24-hour sample plus S3 link for docs?
[03:31] Marcus: Yes, I'll get that by EOD tomorrow.
[03:34] Samir: Great. A few technical clarifications — how important is strict data residency?
[03:38] Priya: EU customer subset requires data to stay in EU. So for those accounts we'd prefer Private in EU region or Dedicated in EU with controls.
[03:46] Lina: We can pin regions and set routing by policy. Also audit logs and token-level tracing are available in Redwood Console.
[03:53] Priya: About model size — is quantization supported? We might want 4-bit to reduce cost.
[03:58] Lina: Yes, the runtime supports quantization paths; but quantization sometimes affects multilingual fluency. We'll recommend model-aware quant profiles.
[04:07] Elena: Any gotchas with retrieval plus tool-calling?
[04:10] Lina: Think about injection and stale retrieval; use RAG with provenance and soft-fallbacks. Also you may want to cache KV responses — I keep saying KV "cash" because of the transcript. Our prefix/KV caching can save cost but must be tuned for your TTLs.
[04:26] Jared: For the pilot, we want Redwood Hosted first for quick results then move to Dedicated/private. Is that typical?
[04:32] Samir: Yes — very common. Start hosted for rapid iteration then Dedicated for production. Private only for regulated enterprise.
[04:37] Priya: We'll want to run a 1-week pilot that includes Spanish/Portuguese workloads, 10k long-doc cases, and some function-calling.
[04:44] Lina: Sounds good. We'll size the hardware and estimate costs.
[04:47] Marcus: Regarding network egress — if we run in our VPC, do you need outbound access?
[04:51] Lina: Minimal for control plane; for fully air-gapped we provide on-prem package. We'll document firewall rules.
[04:57] Samir: Ok next steps recap — we'll send pricing & pilot terms, Lina will coordinate benchmark plan, Marcus will provide sample traffic. Any other blockers?
[05:05] Jared: SOC2 evidence — if you could share that plus KMS/HSM integration notes that would help legal.
[05:11] Samir: Absolutely. I'll attach SOC2 + encryption docs.
[05:14] Elena: Also please include a short sample of the eval harness and a couple example prompts we can run.
[05:19] Lina: Will do.
[05:21] (brief silence)
[05:28] Priya: One last technical point — do you support function calling with structured outputs? We want JSON schema adherence.
[05:34] Lina: Yes, function-calling supports structured responses, and we can do schema validation with strict outputs. We'll demo in the benchmark.
[05:40] Samir: Perfect. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window. Thank you all.
[05:45] Jared: Thanks everyone.
[05:48] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., KV cache spelled as KV cash), some proper nouns may be auto-corrected. Links shared verbally are noted above.

Referenced docs and artifacts: Redwood security pack (link provided in next steps), sample eval harness (will be shared), pricing sheet (to be sent).
